reason: I install new tools on a whim, so I'll definitely try it, but FastStone already does my full-screen browsing, resizing and quick edits and I have no real problem with it. One developer and version 0.4.1 isn't enough for me to hand over my default.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers are nice, but my photos are phone shots and screenshots, and FastStone is fast enough on those. The thing that would pull me in is the Space-bar preview from Explorer and the screenshot importer, if they work well. I wouldn't switch until I know my phone photos open, and HEIC needing Microsoft's HEVC extension is a red flag. I also doubt its editor can replace the FastStone editor I use every day.
current_app_pros: FastStone's full-screen mode, thumbnail browser and simple editor (resize, crop, annotate, red-eye) are all in one place and I know them by heart. It opens my phone photos, screenshots and the odd PDF without fuss, and it's been stable for years.
current_app_pains: Nothing big. It looks dated and it's a little slow when I flick through a lot of pictures quickly. Some of the odd formats a friend sends don't open.
objection: Will my phone photos (HEIC) and my camera RAW open correctly, and will the editor do what I do in FastStone? I've also seen one-person viewers get abandoned, so I don't want to move my whole routine over to something that may stop being updated.
would_change_my_mind: I'd switch if my phone HEIC photos and RAW files open correctly with no extra setup, and I could do my daily FastStone edits (resize, crop, annotate) in it. A few months of steady updates would also help.
